record.context_brief: Reducing subspaces for the weighted composition semigroup
record.original_question: Let W = (W_n)_{n≥1} be the semigroup of weighted composition operators on the Hardy-Hilbert space H^2 defined by W_n f(z) = (1 + z + · · · + z^{n−1})f(z^n). For each k ≥ 2 define h_k(z) = (1/(1 − z)) log((1 + z + · · · + z^{k−1})/k), and let N := span{h_k : k ≥ 2}. Is the closure of N invariant under W_n^* for some n ≥ 2? Equivalently, does the closure of N reduce W_n for some n ≥ 2?

evidence.quote: For each k ≥ 2, define h_k(z) = 1/(1 − z) log((1 + z + · · · + z^{k−1})/k) and let N := span{h_k : k ≥ 2}.
In [16], a semigroup of weighted composition operators W = (W_n)_{n∈N} on H^2 was introduced, where W_n f(z) = (1 + z + . . . + z^{n−1})f(z^n) = (1 − z^n)/(1 − z) f(z^n).
We know that the closure of N is invariant under W_n for all n ∈ N. Is the closure of N also invariant under any W^*_n, equivalently, does the closure of N reduce any W_n.
Theorem 12. The closure of N reduces W_n for some n ≥ 2 if and only if the RH is true.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $H^2$ denote the Hardy-Hilbert space of analytic functions on the open unit disk $\mathbb{D}$ with square-summable Taylor coefficients. For each integer $n \ge 1$, define the weighted composition operator $W_n : H^2 \to H^2$ by
$$ (W_n f)(z) \;=\; (1 + z + z^2 + \cdots + z^{n-1})\, f(z^n) \;=\; \frac{1-z^n}{1-z}\, f(z^n). $$
The family $W = (W_n)_{n \ge 1}$ forms a semigroup under composition. For each integer $k \ge 2$ set
$$ h_k(z) \;=\; \frac{1}{1-z}\,\log\!\left(\frac{1 + z + z^2 + \cdots + z^{k-1}}{k}\right), \qquad z \in \mathbb{D}, $$
and let $N := \operatorname{span}\{ h_k : k \ge 2 \} \subset H^2$. It is known that the closure $\overline{N}$ in $H^2$ is invariant under $W_n$ for every $n \ge 1$.

Question: Does there exist an integer $n \ge 2$ such that $\overline{N}$ is invariant under the adjoint $W_n^*$ (equivalently, such that $\overline{N}$ reduces $W_n$)?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is equivalent to the Riemann Hypothesis: it has been shown that the closure of $N$ reduces $W_n$ for some $n \ge 2$ if and only if RH holds. Since RH remains unresolved, this problem is open.

status_evidence.title: Riemann Hypothesis - Clay Mathematics Institute
status_evidence.snippet: The Riemann Hypothesis is one of the seven Millennium Prize Problems and remains unsolved.
status_evidence.claim: RH is still open, so the equivalent reducing-subspace question is open as well.
